findings.trigger: Application app-1 tailored once (SPEND for app-1, keywordCoverage.final set). User edits the profile and taps Re-tailor (W4-D1) or goes back from Tailored to Quick question, changes the answer and continues (W4-B2): TailoringNavKey(app-1) -> alreadySpent && final != null -> Success without running, so the stale resume is shown and the profile/answer change is ignored. If the quick-question save recomputes coverage with KeywordCoverageCalculator.compute(matches, answer, null) (as #276 does at creation), final is null and the runner tailors again WITHOUT spending: a free re-tailor in demo, and in prod a local ledger that misses the server debit. W4-D1 owns only feature/applications/impl/** and cannot fix this.
findings.title: Spend idempotency keyed on applicationId makes every re-tailor of the same application a no-op or free
findings.proof: TailoringRunnerTest: run the runner for app-1, then upsert app-1 with an edited quickAnswer (or seed a changed profile) and run it again as a new run; assert the second run calls tailoring and the ledger has 2 SPEND rows — today reruns == 0 and 1 row. Fix: give each run an id: TailoringNavKey(applicationId, runId) with runId = idGenerator.newId() at the Tailor/Re-tailor tap (TailorFailedNavigation.retry reuses key.runId; the key is saved with the back stack, so it survives process death); record runId on the SPEND row (new CreditLedgerEntry.runId, or productId for SPEND rows) and on the application with the result; alreadySpent = ledger.any { SPEND && runId == key.runId }; return Success without a run only when application.tailoringRunId == key.runId.

Fix: val summaryHighlight = resume.summary?.takeIf { it.decision == ACCEPTED }?.let { if (it.sourceIds.any { id -> id.startsWith(ANSWER_ID_PREFIX) }) FromAnswer else FromResume } ?: TmrPaperHighlight.None.
